claims.text: Nicotine replacement (gum, lozenge, patch, nasal spray) is designed to reduce withdrawal;
claims.quote: Nicotine replacement products are designed to reduce withdrawal when quitting smoking. Four nicotine replacement therapies (in the form of gum, lozenges, transdermal patch, and nasal spray

claims.text: the US nicotine inhaler was discontinued in 2023.
claims.quote: the nicotine inhaler was discontinued in the United States in 2023

claims.text: Combining the patch with a shorter-acting form is more effective than one product and comparable to varenicline;
claims.quote: combinations of different nicotine replacement products are more effective than single products and are comparable in efficacy to varenicline (5). For example, combining the nicotine patch with a shorter-acting nicotine replacement drug (eg, lozenge, gum, nasal spray) is more effective than monotherapy.

claims.text: dose about 1 mg of nicotine replacement per cigarette smoked a day.
claims.quote: Nicotine replacement therapy is dosed at about 1 mg of nicotine replacement per cigarette smoked per day.

claims.text: Varenicline is a partial agonist/antagonist at the alpha-4 beta-2 nicotinic receptor;
claims.quote: Varenicline works at the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (the alpha-4 beta-2 subunit), where it acts as a partial agonist, having some nicotinic effects, and as a partial antagonist, blocking the effects of nicotine.

claims.text: it eases withdrawal and blunts the reward of a lapse,
claims.quote: The effect of varenicline is to mitigate nicotine withdrawal symptoms and decrease the pleasurable effects of smoking if the patient has a lapse.

claims.text: and is the most effective monotherapy.
claims.quote: Varenicline is the most effective monotherapy available for smoking cessation
